_readme: SEED FILE. `scripts/seed.ts` is the only code path that opens this
directory, and nothing here is read at runtime: Postgres is the
single source of truth once a row lands, so an edit below changes
nothing until the next seed pass applies it.
Keys beginning with an underscore are stripped by the loader before
anything is validated or written, which is what lets a seed file
carry this header at all. A seed is usually met on its own, in a
diff or an editor tab, where nothing about the content says which
path owns it.
This file seeds `terms`. A term is upserted by the (category,
pattern) pair `terms_category_id_pattern_unique` holds, so a second
seed pass rewrites a term's weight and polarity rather than adding
a second row that would then count the same match twice.
`categoryKey` is not a column. `terms.category_id` holds a key the
database issues, and no seed file can know one before the category
row is written, so a term names its category by the key
`categories.json` seeds. The loader resolves it, and refuses a term
naming a key the bundle does not carry.
What that member does not carry is the other half of a category's
natural key. A category is identified by (domain, key), and the
bundle holds one domain today, so a key names one row. A second
domain reusing `technologies` would make this member ambiguous
without making it unresolved — the loader holds a `categoryKey`
against every key the bundle declares, so both categories would
answer to it and neither would be reported. Whoever adds that
domain owns the choice.
`weight` is magnitude only. Which way a match points is
`polarity`'s to say, and the sign written here is not consulted, so
a negative number would mean exactly what its positive means. The
two are separate columns for that reason, and no row below infers
either from the other.
`polarity` is one of `positive`, `negative` or `ignore` — the set
`terms_polarity_check` holds, generated from `TERM_POLARITIES` in
`src/db/schema/values.ts`. Every category below carries all three,
so the worked example exercises the whole set rather than the two
members a shorter list would reach, and its three `ignore` rows are
there for three different reasons: a pattern that matches
everything, one suspended with its weight intact, and one
considered and left neutral.
Nothing in the schema says what an `ignore` row's weight should be,
and the rows below keep the magnitude they would carry under a
different polarity rather than flattening it to zero. Suspending or
restoring a term is then one UPDATE of one column, with no second
decision to re-take. Whether a matcher consults a suspended row's
weight is the matcher's decision and not this file's; the matcher
arrives with the scoring port in phase 5.
`notes` is nullable and written out on every row, null included, so
a row with nothing recorded is distinguishable from a member
somebody left off. The rows carrying prose are the ones whose
direction would otherwise read as arbitrary — the negative and the
ignore ones — while a positive term at an ordinary weight explains
itself.
The patterns are illustrative, like the rest of
`example-tech-radar`: kinds of technology rather than products, and
sectors rather than positions on them. A term pointing away from
something records the example's own stated preference and is not a
recommendation this repository makes. Real vocabulary belongs to
whoever operates an instance and reaches the database through their
own seeds.

terms.notes: Illustrative: this example's radar prefers technology it can run without a vendor relationship.
Matches nearly every document this domain reads, so it sorts nothing. Kept as a row rather than deleted, so the next reader meets a pattern that was considered and not one that was missed.
The strongest signal in this example: a document announcing one is describing something the radar can stop following.
Suspended rather than removed — it turned up on both sides often enough to separate nothing. The weight is the one it carried, so restoring it is an edit to this row's polarity alone.
Illustrative only. A radar narrows what it reads by naming sectors it is not following; the row shows that shape and makes no claim about the sector.
Considered and left neutral: documents from this sector are read like any other. The row is what lets the next reader tell a decision from an omission.
